    my $z = length("abc")-length("a"); print "$z\n";

A SPACE fixes it (`) - length(`); `)-1` is already repaired (PPI-bugs section 15) and `)*name` is already repaired (section 12).  This is the third sibling and it is UNREPAIRED.

PPI 1.291 token dump:

    length ( "abc" )   Word(-length)   ( "a" )        <- WRONG (one Word)
    length ( "abc" )   Operator(-) Word(length) ...   <- right, with a space

perl: after `)` a term has ENDED, so `-` is subtraction; `-bareword` (the string form) can only start where a TERM can.  Exactly the section 12/15 rule.

Both are silent today (module mode announces nothing).  This is why the shape has never appeared in the drop census: the census does not cover the module populations (#462).
